items.stem: Which TWO statements about capacity factor are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is the ratio of actual energy output to the output at full nameplate capacity over a period
options.rationale: That is the definition of capacity factor.

options.text: A higher capacity factor means the plant delivered more of its theoretical maximum
options.rationale: Correct: it measures how fully the capacity was used.

options.text: It is always equal to the plant's thermal efficiency
options.rationale: Capacity factor and thermal efficiency are different quantities.

options.text: It can exceed 100% for renewable plants
options.rationale: Output cannot exceed the nameplate maximum over the same period.

items.explanation: That is the definition of capacity factor.

items.stem: A country's total primary energy use is flat but peak electricity demand is climbing. What best explains this?

options.text: Electrification and shifting daily usage patterns raise peaks even when total energy is steady
options.rationale: Peak power depends on simultaneous demand, which can rise independently of annual totals.

options.text: The country is using more energy overall
options.rationale: The premise states total energy use is flat.

options.text: Capacity factors of all plants have fallen to zero
options.rationale: That would cut output, not raise demand peaks.

options.text: Energy and power are the same quantity
options.rationale: They are distinct; peaks are a power measure, totals an energy measure.

items.explanation: Peak power depends on simultaneous demand, which can rise independently of annual totals.
